core_axes.1_inciting_disruption: Her twin Cora lived in the house as 'Maud' for nine weeks, impersonating her in person at Friday dinners before Declan's boss, colleagues and the neighbours, with Declan complicit from the first night (he 'poured the wine'); Cora also used Maud's phone to send forged emails withdrawing her from the parish contract and resigning to her mentor. Maud discovers it unseen, from across the street through the dining-room window, the night before their anniversary (Ch1).
core_axes.2_the_bind: Leaving the house is easy but leaving the problem is not: the forged resignation has cost her the St. Wenceslaus commission and her mentor's trust, a Christmas Eve re-dedication needs independent certification, her plated right hand trembles at fine work, and every other pair of steady hands is either in Boston or has heard from Frances that she quit, so the only hands she can command without asking a favour are her husband's.
core_axes.3_first_irreversible_decision: Ch3: on their anniversary morning she works her house key off the ring left-handed, leaves it beside his unopened gift and moves to a cot in her unheated studio; Ch6 she then signs a no-deposit, certification-conditional contract left-handed, staking her name on five weeks.
core_axes.4_midpoint_reversal: Chs 11-15: both admit they were relieved by the absence (she glad to be away, he 'stopped waiting for you' at the Valley Forge exit), then Odalys's screenshots, the confrontation with their mother and Frances reading the forged resignation aloud show the real theft was her professional name, not the house; Frances sets terms (Maud in arm's reach, awake, every swab logged).
core_axes.5_rupture_lowest_point: Chs 18-19: while she sleeps he 'takes it off her plate', cleans a corner alone in breach of Frances's one-entry rule and removes 13 mm of irreplaceable 1886 glaze ('This is what you do. You make it easier, and it's gone'); in Ch23 a wrist screw backs out and she ends the terms and empties the phone bowl.
core_axes.6_climax_action: Ch27: Declan cleans the Virgin's face in six 90-second sections on Maud's spoken count while Frances watches; he says his hand is tired between sections, and on her pre-planned 'Leave it' he stops a millimetre short of the old brow damage. Frances reads the hinged confession page in the log and certifies. Caused jointly, set in motion by Maud asking rather than ordering (Ch26).
core_axes.7_repair_mechanism: Changed behaviour: phone and watch in her bowl every shift; he does only what he's told; writes up his own damage in his capitals for her, Frances and the Monsignor to read; tells Ray, the office floor and the neighbours the truth in person; refuses Pauline's offer to blame Cora; turns down Atlanta for 'evenings' (Ray, Nadine and later Joan witness it); answers 'Ask Maud' before the Commission; says 'my hand's tired' in front of Frances; asks 'What do you need?' twice. She resumes asking him for things.
core_axes.8_resolution_epilogue_shape: Ch28 cot scene: the apology he wasn't allowed to give is finally allowed, she lists the things she'll ask him for, one kiss, the house key back on her ring, the July magnifier gift finally opened. Ch29: hanging and Midnight Mass, he stays out of every photograph, she tells Cora on the steps 'March. Bring nothing.' Ch30 (March): a Saturday at a shared bench, he cleaning a $4 cow painting, Cora silent on the stool, ending on 'Again.'

first_attraction_device.quote: Inside the black brace on my other wrist my pulse had come up hard against the plastic... I had stopped at forty-one. The timer had not. (Ch9)

first_care_device.quote: “She needs them,” he said, which was the reason he’d ordered them. (Ch2: headband magnifiers ordered in July, wrapped badly himself)

core_axes.inciting_disruption: Investor-partner Porter redirects Marisol's correctly answered draw-schedule question to Idris in a client meeting before Renata Cho (Ch1) and Idris does not notice; on a recorded conference call (Ch3) the client herself says Marisol built the systems while Idris stays silent, then texts her only 'good call'.
core_axes.the_bind: She signed the personal loan guarantee on the Brenner Row project, is unsalaried in a family company she rescued after an embezzlement six years earlier, holds the systems eleven employees' jobs depend on, and shares a fifteen-year marriage, a home and a fourteen-year-old daughter, with her own design studio packed in a storage unit.
core_axes.first_irreversible_decision: Ch4: she refuses to finish the Friday underwriting package unless her name goes on the client-facing team, openly accepting the risk of losing the locked loan rate ('I would rather lose four points on a loan').
core_axes.midpoint_reversal: Ch13: Idris surprises her at a restaurant with a Director of Operations title, a 15% retroactive raise and a bracelet; she refuses the shape of it ('generosity that gets decided for somebody instead of with them is just control with better lighting'), moving the problem from credit to inclusion, and he then starts a secret equity negotiation with the lawyer and Porter (Ch14-16).
core_axes.rupture_lowest_point: Ch18: at the Friday all-hands Idris announces her 10% ownership stake, negotiated for six weeks without her, to applause; she does not clap, their daughter hears it from a classmate, and the deadline on her rival partnership offer lapses unanswered while she sits in the storage-unit lot (Ch18C-19).
core_axes.climax_action: Heroine-caused: she catches an egress-code violation in Porter's corridor cut, which makes him name her on the record before the bonding committee (Ch20-20B); then in the site trailer (Ch23) she lays Celeste's signed offer on the desk, Idris confesses his Seattle visit before she speaks, and she declines the offer and dictates her terms while he writes them down and leaves the envelope unopened.
core_axes.repair_mechanism: Idris writes her list of his wrongs on legal pads; she redlines the equity agreement in the lawyer's office and strikes his sole-tiebreaker clause (witnessed by Ellen, with Porter agreeing to quiet written disclosure); he brings licensing facts instead of plans and asks before acting on clients and hires; he stays deliberately silent while she runs the final walkthrough (witnessed by Renata and Porter); the company is renamed Calder & Vega.
core_axes.resolution_epilogue_shape: Four months later: the CALDER & VEGA CONSTRUCTION sign goes up in his father's typeface while family and Deb watch; she has a windowed office, her drafting table and three design clients, has stopped counting smile seconds, and walks out hand in hand with Idris.

core_axes.inciting_disruption: A florist's assistant, by phone, tells Ines alone in her kitchen that 'his office' (assistant Fern Alcott) calls in the anniversary order every year; next morning Fern confirms by phone in the school parking lot that she has written every card, picked every gift and dinner, and booked Margo's medical care for eight years. There is no audience and no affair.
core_axes.the_bind: Nothing external holds her: she still loves the actual man, and Naomi lists what leaving would cost (half the house, no credit for 18 months of unpaid early bookkeeping for Calloway Freight, a principal's social exposure in a small town). So she binds herself with a one-year deadline that has a real divorce consequence.
core_axes.first_irreversible_decision: Ch 4: she hands Whit the six-page list 'EVERYTHING I HAVE BEEN RUNNING', removes Fern from the shared marriage calendar in front of him through three confirmation screens, has already moved Margo's cardiology contact off Fern, and sets one year with a filing with Naomi as the price. Her visible price is giving up her own safety-net role, so nobody covers the dropped tasks.
core_axes.midpoint_reversal: Ch 22-24: Whit nearly forgets Margo's birthday, catches it at 4:40pm, and tells her the truth that he almost forgot, without calling Ines or Fern. Ines then catches herself texting that she had booked the gutter cleaners, Naomi names it as the same overfunctioning habit, and the repair becomes two-sided rather than his alone.
core_axes.rupture_lowest_point: Ch 39-40, nine days before the deadline: Margo falls while the Vance team has flown in unannounced to force a decision. Whit says 'I'm going to send Fern' and stays 90 more minutes to close a three-year renewal. Fern goes out of love for Margo, not for him. Whit arrives at 4:55pm, and in Margo's driveway admits 'I failed the test.'
core_axes.climax_action: Ch 44: a reefer unit fails on the first Berkline load and Roland Vance demands Whit in person. Whit decides overnight, with Ines deliberately giving no advice, to have COO Deborah lead the response and not fly. He invites Ines to his office at about 8am and phones Roland on speaker with her as the only witness, stating the real reason (the anniversary and his mother's fall). Roland laughs and says 'Send Deborah... Happy anniversary.' Whit causes the outcome and Ines witnesses it.
core_axes.repair_mechanism: Self-performed care done badly and repeated, witnessed mostly by Ines and Margo: he attends Lila's concert alone with his phone left in the car, cooks Thanksgiving, burns the chicken at Margo's, sorts Desmond's study himself, and calls the Ashworths. He also arranges Deshawn's rides and tells no one; Ines learns of it by accident. Further acts: the six o'clock phone rule, data entry for her audit, the leave-by-six company policy (witnessed by employees), and promoting Deborah. Client Roland Vance and his wife Cheryl independently notice the change.
core_axes.resolution_epilogue_shape: There is no epilogue. Ch 45: his prepared index-card apology collapses after card seven into a plain 'I let you disappear', and she answers 'I love you' with their first kiss of the year. Ch 46, the anniversary Saturday: a card in his own hand misspelling 'deserve'. Margo hands over Desmond's box of cards. Ines overhears, unseen, Whit confirm Margo's appointment and make himself the contact, a callback to ch 4. They walk out to two cars with no plan.

first_attraction_quote: looking, for all the world, like someone who had shown up somewhere on time because he wanted to be there and not because anyone had told him to. (ch 5, Ines watching from the back row before he sees her)
first_care_quote: carrying a bag from the good Thai place, the one three towns over that I loved and he found mediocre and always ordered from anyway because I loved it. (ch 2, immediately undercut: she wonders whether that too 'had gone out under someone else's name')
